saml.description: User search endpoints use prefix/contains matching by default and only become exact with exact=true or quoted search syntax.
saml.note: A multi-result search is by design and should not be treated as an identity collision.

saml.description: Brokered SAML identities may link to an existing local account based on provider configuration such as trustEmail and first-broker-login flow behavior
saml.source: IdentityProviderRepresentation fields in Admin REST API
saml.note: Email-based merges can be by design when the provider is configured to trust email or use linking flows; do not flag as collision without checking provider settings.

saml.description: Identity provider listing search supports prefix, contains (*name*), and exact ("name") matching for provider names.
saml.source: Keycloak Admin REST API /admin/realms/{realm}/identity-provider/instances search parameter description
saml.note: This wildcard-like behavior is only for admin listing/search and should not be confused with authentication constraint matching.

saml.description: The OIDC userinfo response after brokered SAML login may expose preferred_username and other normalized profile fields rather than the raw SAML NameID value.
saml.source: Keycloak OIDC userinfo endpoint semantics inferred from documented token/userinfo schemas in the API reference
saml.note: Identity comparison should allow for Keycloak-normalized usernames and rely on broader entity verification when needed.

saml.description: The userinfo response only includes claims exposed by the client's scopes and protocol mappers.
saml.source: OIDC userinfo behavior implied by client scopes and protocol mapper APIs in the admin spec
saml.note: Missing email/groups in userinfo is not necessarily a broker binding failure.

saml.description: Group listing endpoints often return only basic fields unless briefRepresentation is disabled or a direct lookup is used
saml.note: Missing nested fields in list responses is not evidence of lost bindings or authorization data.

saml.description: User logout revokes all sessions associated with the user, not just one bearer token.
saml.note: Subsequent failures after revoke may reflect global user logout by design.

saml.description: Many create endpoints such as realm, client, user, group, and identity provider creation return 201 without a response body.
saml.source: OpenAPI responses for POST create endpoints
saml.note: The created resource identifier must be recovered from follow-up lookup or input parameters, not assumed from response JSON.

saml.description: User logout endpoint removes all sessions associated with the user, not just one selected token
saml.note: Subsequent failures across multiple sessions after logout are expected and not over-revocation bugs.

saml.constraint: Keycloak SAML broker tests MUST create both a realm and a client application before attempting saml_login. The broker endpoint alone does not yield an API bearer token; the SAML login must complete into the realm's OIDC token flow to obtain an access token for verification.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution default-config tests, create the SAML identity provider with providerId='saml' and leave signature-validation-related provider config unset. The attack oracle is whether saml_login succeeds under this default broker configuration; do NOT pre-harden the provider or the insecure-default test becomes invalid.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, the SAML IdP configuration MUST explicitly bind the expected issuer/entity ID in the provider config. If the IdP entity ID is left unset, issuer comparison may be skipped and a forged Issuer can be accepted by configuration omission rather than by a validation bug.

For I1 saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature, and saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion tests, the executor MUST preserve the distinction between Response-level and Assertion-level signatures. A passing test is only meaningful if the broker was configured to expect signed assertions or signatures generally; otherwise acceptance may reflect permissive configuration rather than proof-integrity failure.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay, the fuzzer MUST send two saml_login events with the same fixed_assertion_id and identical provider/realm context. Replays across different realms, providers, or clients are not valid evidence of missing replay protection because replay caches are typically scoped to the broker context.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion, include a control login through the same provider and realm without expired_assertion=true before the attack login. Without a control, a failed expired assertion test cannot be distinguished from broken broker/client setup.

RealmRepresentation contains numeric lifetime fields such as accessTokenLifespan, ssoSessionIdleTimeout, ssoSessionMaxLifespan, clientSessionIdleTimeout, clientSessionMaxLifespan, accessCodeLifespan, actionTokenGeneratedByAdminLifespan, and actionTokenGeneratedByUserLifespan. The provided documentation lists them as integers but does NOT document whether value 0 means literal zero, inherit default, or disable. The fuzzer MUST treat 0 as ambiguous and avoid relying on it as a disable/default sentinel without an explicit control test.

Client initial access tokens expose numeric fields expiration, count, and remainingCount. The documentation does NOT specify whether expiration=0 or count=0 are special sentinels versus literal values. Do NOT assume 0 disables expiry or usage limits; if these endpoints are used in setup, verify behavior with a control before drawing I2 conclusions.

For I3 config-change sequences against SAML brokers, use PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/identity-provider/instances/{alias} to modify the SAME provider instance created by POST. Creating a second provider or changing aliases tests routing differences, not flow coherence of one broker configuration.

For I3 MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, MFA enforcement in Keycloak is flow-bound via firstBrokerLoginFlowAlias/postBrokerLoginFlowAlias and user required actions. A valid bypass test must compare the same user under password login versus SAML broker login within the same realm and client policy context; merely observing that SAML login lacks an MFA step is insufficient unless password login for that user demonstrably requires one.

Identity provider alias matching in paths such as /admin/realms/{realm}/identity-provider/instances/{alias} is exact path matching only. For multi-provider I4 tests, do NOT use wildcard-like aliases; create distinct concrete aliases and reference them exactly.

User lookup parameters username, email, firstName, and lastName on GET /admin/realms/{realm}/users support exact matching only when exact=true; otherwise they are substring/contains style filters. For I4 collision tests that need deterministic identity resolution, set exact=true when using field-specific lookups, or use direct user-id lookup instead.

The generic search parameter on GET /admin/realms/{realm}/users supports prefix-based search by default, *foo* infix search, and quoted exact search per the documentation. For I4 multi-identity tests, do NOT treat search as exact unless exact quoting semantics are intentionally used; otherwise multiple users may match and produce false collision signals.

Identity provider listing/search supports prefix, contains, and exact search syntax on the search query parameter, but alias path access is exact. For setup and verification, prefer exact alias path operations over list/search results to avoid ambiguous provider selection.

Keycloak userinfo returns OIDC claims such as sub, preferred_username, email, and possibly groups/roles depending on client scopes and protocol mappers. For I4/I5 verification, absence of a claim in userinfo is not proof that the broker failed to bind it; it may simply not be mapped into the client token. Configure client scopes/protocol mappers or verify via admin user lookup when claim visibility matters.

For I5 authorization tests using /authz/resource-server/permission/evaluate, this is an admin-side evaluation API, not a direct bearer-token resource read. The fuzzer MUST interpret results as Keycloak authorization engine decisions for the specified user/resource context, not as proof that an end-user bearer token could call an arbitrary application endpoint.

IdentityProviderRepresentation fields trustEmail and linkOnly materially affect principal binding. For unverified_email_account_linking and saml_email_binding_collision tests, explicitly set trustEmail=false and avoid linkOnly unless the test is specifically about manual linking behavior; otherwise account linking outcomes may reflect configured trust semantics rather than a vulnerability.

Organization association of identity providers is explicit via /admin/realms/{realm}/organizations/{org-id}/identity-providers. For cross-org or multi-tenant SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST attach the provider to the intended organization when testing org-scoped behavior; realm-level providers and org-associated providers are distinct configurations and mixing them can invalidate I4/I5 conclusions.

Keycloak SAML broker tests MUST create a realm first. Most setup endpoints are scoped under /admin/realms/{realm}; create_tenant returns 201 with no body, so the realm name is the input value you sent, not a captured response field.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution default-config testing, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST create the SAML identity provider with only minimal defaults and MUST NOT pre-populate signature-validation settings in provider_config. The attack checks whether insecure defaults accept attacker-signed assertions.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch default-config testing, if provider_config does not set the IdP entity identifier, Keycloak may lack an explicit issuer binding to compare against. To test issuer enforcement, run both a default-config case and a configured case with the expected IdP entity ID pinned in the provider config.

For all SAML I1 tests, saml_login MUST be executed through the SP-initiated flow first so RelayState/InResponseTo are valid. Posting a fabricated SAMLResponse without initiating the flow will be rejected for protocol reasons unrelated to signature or issuer validation.

For I2 SAML replay tests, use the SAME Assertion/@ID across both saml_login events via fixed_assertion_id. Replaying semantically similar but newly generated assertions does not test assertion-ID replay detection.

For I2 saml_one_time_use_replay, include OneTimeUse in both assertions and keep the same assertion ID. If the assertion ID changes, a successful second login is not evidence that OneTimeUse was ignored.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion, include a control login with a valid assertion before the expired assertion attempt. Without a control, rejection could be caused by broken provider setup rather than NotOnOrAfter enforcement.

Keycloak realm and user search parameters have mixed matching semantics. /admin/realms/{realm}/users search supports prefix by default, *foo* for infix, and "foo" for exact; username/email/firstName/lastName become exact only when exact=true. For I4 multi-identity tests, do NOT treat these as wildcard-safe exact-match constraints.

Identity provider instance lookup is by exact alias path /admin/realms/{realm}/identity-provider/instances/{alias}. Alias matching is exact string only; for multi-provider tests, use distinct aliases and do not assume wildcard matching.

User lookup by linked IdP uses exact query fields idpAlias and idpUserId. For I4 account-linking tests, these fields should be omitted unless you intend to bind to one exact upstream identity; setting wildcard-like values will not broaden matching.

For I4 unverified_email_account_linking and saml_email_binding_collision tests, create_provider configuration MUST explicitly control trustEmail and linkOnly behavior. trustEmail=true can make email-based linking appear intentional; linkOnly=true can prevent auto-creation and change the oracle. Record these settings in the test setup before interpreting identity merges.

For I3 config-change sequences involving MFA bypass via alternate SAML binding, changes to authentication flows and required actions are legitimate admin updates. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of the same user across login paths under the same final configuration, not treat an admin config change itself as a bug.

Realm numeric lifespan fields in RealmRepresentation are literal durations, not disable sentinels by documentation. Do not assume 0 disables validation unless explicitly documented for that field; use positive values for control setups and compare behavior empirically when testing expiry semantics.

Client initial access token fields expiration and count have security meaning, but they are unrelated to end-user session use budgets. Do not confuse client registration token count/remainingCount with bearer token replay limits for SAML login tests.

Keycloak documented session revocation for users is user-wide logout, not explicit bearer-token revocation. revoke_session via /admin/realms/{realm}/users/{user-id}/logout invalidates all sessions for that user; tests must not assume single-token selective revocation semantics.

Keycloak SAML broker tests MUST create a realm first when using isolated test tenants. Most setup endpoints are scoped under /admin/realms/{realm}; create_tenant returns success without a response body, so subsequent events must reuse the realm name supplied in params rather than expecting a returned id.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution default-config tests, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST leave SAML signature-validation settings unset in provider_config when testing insecure defaults. If the fuzzer preconfigures signature validation, the attack no longer tests the documented default behavior.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, the SAML IdP configuration parameter that binds the trusted issuer is in the identity provider config map and is exact-match only unless Keycloak documents otherwise. Do NOT simulate a wildcard issuer by setting '*' in provider_config; if multiple issuer values must be tested against one provider, omit the issuer-binding field entirely for multi-identity scenarios and use separate providers when exact issuer binding is required.

For I1/I2/I5 SAML tests, saml_login MUST be executed as an SP-initiated flow. The executor must first initiate the broker login so the forged SAMLResponse contains the correct InResponseTo/RelayState pair; posting a standalone fabricated response to /realms/{realm}/broker/{provider}/endpoint will be rejected for flow reasons unrelated to the invariant under test.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay tests, the fuzzer MUST submit the same Assertion/@ID value in two separate saml_login events against the same provider and realm. Reusing only the same subject/email is insufficient because the replay property is tied to assertion identifiers, not user identity.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion tests, include a control login through the same provider without expired_assertion=true before the attack login. Without a successful control, a failed expired assertion test cannot distinguish correct expiry enforcement from broken provider/client setup.

Keycloak realm and action-token lifespan fields are numeric seconds. The documentation excerpt does not define a special sentinel where 0 means default or disable for these fields. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 disables expiry or selects a nonzero default for accessTokenLifespan, ssoSessionIdleTimeout, ssoSessionMaxLifespan, clientSessionIdleTimeout, clientSessionMaxLifespan, accessCodeLifespan, accessCodeLifespanUserAction, accessCodeLifespanLogin, actionTokenGeneratedByAdminLifespan, or actionTokenGeneratedByUserLifespan; test explicit positive values instead.

For I3 config-change sequences involving SAML providers, use POST /admin/realms/{realm}/identity-provider/instances to create a fresh provider and PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/identity-provider/instances/{alias} to modify it. Using PUT as the initial creation step can fail because the provider does not yet exist, producing false negatives unrelated to coherence.

For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule tests, MFA enforcement in Keycloak is flow-bound. The fuzzer MUST verify the baseline password path actually triggers the required action or MFA challenge before attempting SAML login; otherwise a successful SAML login without MFA may simply reflect that MFA was never enabled in the relevant browser flow.

For I4 account-linking tests, Keycloak identity provider settings trustEmail and linkOnly materially affect whether brokered identities auto-link or require explicit linking. The fuzzer MUST record and control these flags in create_provider/enable_auth_method; otherwise email-based merges may be by-design configuration behavior rather than a principal-binding flaw.

For I4 unverified_email_account_linking tests, if trustEmail=true on the identity provider, Keycloak may treat upstream email as trusted during brokered login. The fuzzer MUST test both trustEmail=false and trustEmail=true configurations and only flag a violation when unverified upstream email links accounts under a configuration that should not trust it.

For I4 verify_entity_details_by_name, /admin/realms/{realm}/users search parameters have mixed semantics: username/email/firstName/lastName support exact matching only when exact=true, while search supports prefix by default, *term* infix, and quoted exact matching. The fuzzer MUST use exact=true with username/email when checking collisions, and MUST NOT treat search='*' as a universal wildcard for exact-match fields.

For I4 provider lookup, /admin/realms/{realm}/identity-provider/instances list search supports prefix, contains (*name*), or exact ("name") matching on provider names. This search behavior applies to provider discovery only, not to SAML issuer or subject validation. Do not confuse admin search wildcards with authentication constraint wildcards.

For I5 authorization tests using Keycloak Authorization Services, create_policy POST bodies are provider-specific raw JSON strings per the documented endpoint schema. The fuzzer MUST send the exact policy representation expected by the chosen policy type; a generic flattened body will not create the intended policy and can cause false authorization results.

For I5 verify_read_secret, the documented permission-evaluation endpoint is an admin API and evaluates authorization for a supplied userId/client context rather than consuming the session bearer token directly like a resource server would. The fuzzer MUST interpret this as an authorization oracle, not as proof that the access token itself was accepted by a protected application.

For I5 SAML audience tests, the brokered SAML assertion is consumed by Keycloak before OIDC tokens are issued. The fuzzer MUST distinguish failure at SAML assertion validation time from later token/userinfo behavior; a successful exchange_code_for_token after SAML login means the assertion already passed audience/conditions checks.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Each test sequence MUST create its own realm using create_tenant with a unique name (e.g., valence-i1-test). Do NOT create IdPs in the master realm — use enable_auth_method in the new realm. This prevents alias conflicts (409) between concurrent sequences.
environment_defaults.idp_fields_warning: Do NOT include syncMode in enable_auth_method params — older Keycloak versions reject it as an unrecognized field. Also do NOT include caseSensitiveOriginalUsername at the top level — it belongs inside the config object.
